instructions:
This repository is MadBridge (madv-tui), a governed multi-agent orchestration layer targeting macOS. Two review priorities matter more here than style.

First: environment-dependent behaviour. Code is authored in Linux containers and CI has historically run only on Linux, but the product targets macOS on both arm64 and x86_64. Flag anything whose correctness depends on the host and is not proven on the host it targets — BSD versus GNU tool differences, shell builtins, date/time parsing, path and case sensitivity, sandbox and process-group behaviour, and any assumption that a passing test proves platform support. A real defect shipped this way: a BSD strptime format treated 'Z' as a literal character to match rather than a UTC designator, so a timestamp parsed in local time. Three reviewers read the diff and passed it; it surfaced only when someone ran it on real hardware.

Second: assertions that check shape rather than meaning. Flag tests and gates that would pass for the wrong reason — a conjunction that short-circuits before the assertion that matters, a check whose success depends on a tool being absent from the environment, a count or format validated without validating the value it stands for, and any place a passing result would be indistinguishable from an unexercised one.

Prefer few high-confidence findings over breadth. State the failing input or condition concretely rather than describing a category of risk.

rules.rule: Any assertion about the host platform, architecture, or OS version must read the value it asserts from the running host, not infer it from a sibling value. process.arch reports 'x64' where uname -m reports 'x86_64'; these are not interchangeable in an assertion.
A test that can pass because a dependency, binary, or environment variable is absent is a defect. Flag any assertion whose success path includes the tool under test being unavailable.
Byte-level or length-level equality must be evaluated independently, never placed after another condition in a conjunction that can short-circuit before it runs.

Establish which write-return contract applies before judging short-write handling; the two are not interchangeable. Node's Writable.write() returns a boolean, where false means the chunk was buffered in full and the caller must await 'drain' before writing again — resending any part of it is a duplication bug. Bun.Terminal.write() returns a byte count that may be less than the input length; treating that short count as proof of full delivery, without a measurement establishing the runtime delivered the remainder, is a data-loss bug. In neither case is the return value alone evidence of delivery: require the test to assert eventual delivered length and eventual delivered bytes against the input, independently.
Changing a CI job into a matrix renames its check and silently breaks any branch-protection rule requiring the old name. Flag matrix conversions on jobs whose names may be required checks.
